chapter: Leaving Stuff Smith; Benny Carter and Fletcher Henderson
title: Stuff spends the payroll on a car; the band demands separate checks
summary: Stuff bought a car with a whole payroll, the Chicago union intervened, and Jones asked the booking agent to send individual checks, which Stuff agreed to and then resented.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Getting paid: wages, scale and the pay envelope

blocks.x: To California. So this must have been about '40. This was '40, and a lot of things was happening in that year. And -- no, what happened is that the last job we played was Blatt's Beer Garden, because we was having so much trouble with Stuff. We was working the Sherman Hotel and things like that. He would take the money and buy an automobile, see. Now, when we couldn't pay the hotel bill, why the manager just said, 'Look, you guys have got to pay sometimes. You all haven't paid anything in two weeks, you know.' So now he don't want to hear about what happened with Stuff, you know, that Stuff's not paying off. Stuff went somewhere and bought a car, with the

payroll, the whole payroll. So now we go to the union in Chicago, so the union had him to give all the money to them, and they would pay us off. You know, they would pay us off until he got caught up again, paid up for two weeks, you know, two weeks behind. So then the union -- so then we had all this trouble, so then we said from now on, we told the booking agent, send out individual checks. That's the only way we can make it. We can't make it, because Stuff is subject to take the money and do this anytime, you know. So Stuff said, "That's a good idea. That's a good idea, yeah."
Now, he said it was a good idea, but he didn't really like it. After we started getting paid, after they started sending us out separate checks, then he didn't like it.
It's like he's not the leader.
Yeah. He began to say, "Send me the checks." See, they sent me all the checks and they sent Stuff his, and they sent me the checks for the other boys, you know.

So then I'd give a man his check and Stuff would say, "Now, who's running the band, me?" I said, "Well, you said it was all right, you know, because I'm not going to stay here while you buy automobiles and things, you know. I can't afford this, Stuff."
